changes: p2 Dharmadhara: dropped 'donor' — the colophon calls only the Makhan Bāhāl man dānapati; Dharmadhara keeps scribe ('dharmmadhrakāṃ … likhitayaṃ', '…dharmadhralena … coyā') and owner ('thavata … yayā').
p2 residence and affiliation set to Ratnakīrti Vihāra, which the colophon states ('ratnakṛtivihālayā'), instead of Makhan Bāhāl, which is only given for p1.
p1 name confidence lowered to medium: 'parmmadhra' could be Padmadhara or Paramadhara.
The 'brother_of' relation is kept but marked doubtful: it rests on the corrupt word 'bhābhṛ'.
Place of copying emptied: 'makhanabāhālayā' is the donor's residence; the colophon does not say where the copy was made.
Month normalized to Āṣāḍha; the purpose wording is clarified.

persons.name: Dharmadhara
persons.evidence: vajrācāṛya dharmadhralena, tha(va)ta, vyākhyānayā yayā taco yā julo

purpose: for the scribe's own use in exposition (thavata vyākhyānayā yayā); sponsored by a dānapati
notes: NS 819 = c. 1699 CE. 'ālaṃbhayāña coyā' means 'began and wrote', so the date may be the day copying started. 'parmmadhra' is the Newari scribal shorthand for -dhara: Padmadhara is the more likely reading, but Paramadhara is possible. 'bhābhṛ' is corrupt. It may stand for 'bhrātṛ' (brother), which would make the two Vajrācāryas brothers, but this is uncertain. Makhan Bāhāl in Kathmandu is generally identified with Ratnakīrti Mahāvihāra, so both men probably belonged to the same vihāra. 'sāṃtikra〈〈sa〉〉vaṃ samāga' is unclear: it may refer to a Śāntikara lineage or title. 'vyākhyāna' (exposition) suggests Dharmadhara meant to use the text in teaching; 'reader' is not added because the colophon does not say so explicitly. Whether the dānapati also commissioned the copy is implied, not stated.
